title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Price increase with no promotion; past price hikes show demand drop. Noise-adjusted promotion lift is x1.0, and no past price increase at this level is recorded. Conservative downward adjustment.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 3.2. No events are scheduled. The price is up 3.4% (to $5.72). Past promotions at similar prices show median lift x1.15, but noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0. The same week last year (2025-10-20) sold 2 units (x0.5 vs baseline), and 2024 saw x2.16. However, the noise-adjusted effect of Halloween is x1.0, and no promotion is planned. A price increase typically reduces demand, and no evidence supports a lift. The classical model suggests x1.0, which aligns with weak evidence. No driver justifies a move from 1.0.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.0 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
